title: feat(spec)!: retire seven overdue ADR-0087 D2 conversions from the load path at 18; record why eight stay
body:
Fixes #23487

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

## What

The family closing card for ADR-0087 D2 conversions that were still on the load path at 18 although their window had closed. Every entry now has a verdict: seven are retired from the load path, and eight stay, each with the reason written into its own docblock, including what would have to change for it to retire.

**Retired** (`retiredFromLoadPath: true`, `retiredAfter: '17.7.0'`, the newest published stable release under the `18.0.0-next` label, the same stamp PR #23485 used):

| entry | `toMajor` | refusal an author now meets |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `flow-node-crud-object-alias` | 17 | CRUD node contract, at `config.object`, naming `objectName` |
| `flow-node-crud-filter-alias` | 11 | CRUD node contract, at `config.filters`, naming `filter` |
| `flow-node-notify-config-aliases` | 17 | `notify` contract, at `to` / `subject` / `body` / `url` / nested `source` |
| `flow-node-map-flow-alias` | 17 | `map` contract, at `config.flow`, naming `flowName` |
| `flow-node-subflow-flow-alias` | 17 | `subflow` contract, at `config.flow`, naming `flowName` |
| `flow-node-script-config-aliases` | 17 | `script` contract, at `functionName` / `input`, naming `function` / `inputs` |
| `sharing-rule-access-level-full-to-edit` | 17 | `SharingLevel`, now an `enumWithRetiredValues` whose `full` prescription names `edit` |

Every one of those refusals is now the upgrade prescription: it names the canonical key, the release that refuses the old spelling (`@objectstack/spec 18`), and, for the step-17 entries, `os migrate meta --from 16`. The flow-node prescriptions used to say "the conversion rewrites it at load", which becomes false at authoring once the entry retires. `accessLevel: 'full'` used to get zod's bare `Invalid value 'full'. Expected one of: read, edit.` Each entry has a row in the removal-version pin's `JOIN` (`retired-key-removal-version.pin.test.ts`), so the release each prescription names is derived from the registry, not trusted.

**Kept, with the reason recorded in the docblock:**

| entry | why it stays (measured on this tree) |
|:--|:--|
| `flow-node-http-callout-rename` (11) | `flow.node.type` is an open namespace (ADR-0018): retired, `type: 'http_request'` passes `defineStack` silently. Retiring it needs a decision to reserve retired official names. |
| `page-kind-jsx-to-html` (11) | `'jsx'` is still a declared member of `PageSchema.kind` and of `COMPILED_PAGE_KINDS`: retired, it passes silently. |
| `view-visibleOn-to-visibleWhen` (15) | `visibleOn` is still a declared `[DEPRECATED]` key that the form schemas fold into `visibleWhen` at parse, so retiring the entry alone changes nothing an author can observe. It retires with the alias (a `retiredKey` tombstone). |
| `page-component-visibility-to-visibleWhen` (15) | Same, on `PageComponentSchema.visibility`. |
| `flow-node-wait-event-config-lift` (17) | `wait` has no `config` contract: retired, a loose `config.timerDuration` beside a declared `waitEventConfig` passes silently. Refusing loose keys would also refuse stored flows whose loose key the block shadows (the rehydration seam parses the same schema), which needs a ruling. |
| `flow-node-connector-config-lift` (17) | Same shape: a loose `config.input` beside a complete `connectorConfig` passes silently, and the action would dispatch with no input. |
| `datasource-driver-mongo-to-mongodb` (17) | `'mongo'` is still a legal value, so there is no refusal to hand the author to. Needs a decision: retire the value, or record the entry as permanent. |
| `retry-policy-converged` (17) | The job half alone. This entry writes the pre-17 `maxRetries: 3` / `backoffMultiplier: 2` into a source `job.retryPolicy` that omits them; retired, such a job would silently drop from 3 retries to 0 under the merged defaults, a default flip no gate can see. It can retire once that flip has a ruling for authored sources. (The `retryDelayMs` rename is not a blocker: every surface already refuses it, a `try_catch` node's `config.retry` included, by the `RetryPolicySchema` tombstone. An earlier version of this row said otherwise; that was a wrong reading taken from a node-level parse, corrected at contract review.) |

`conversions.test.ts` holds the verdict list. A new entry below 18 that is neither retired nor on the kept list is an entry nobody judged, and the test goes red on it.

## Enumeration (done before any edit)

Re-derived from `packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts` on `origin/main` `1418de4c7`, by importing `ALL_CONVERSIONS` and keeping every entry whose `toMajor` is below 18 and that carries no `retiredFromLoadPath`: 15 entries (3 at `toMajor: 11`, 2 at 15, 10 at 17). This matches the card's table exactly (10 + 5). There is no difference to report.

## Premise check, per entry (before deciding)

For each entry, `fixture.before` (completed with the labels, flow `type` and `edges` the fixtures leave out) went through `defineStack` twice: once with the entry live, and once with `retiredFromLoadPath` set on it in memory. The issues the second run adds are the answer an author would meet after retirement:

- The six flow-node aliases and `full`: the second run adds a refusal at the old key, naming the canonical key. That is the precondition, met. For `full`, the text was the generic enum message, so the retirement adds the prescription.
- `http_request`, `kind: 'jsx'`, `visibleOn`, `visibility` and `mongo`: the second run adds nothing, so the old spelling would be accepted silently. Kept.
- wait and connector: the second run refuses only when the block is missing, and a loose key beside a declared block passes. Kept.
- retry: `flow.errorHandling.retryDelayMs` is tombstoned, but the `try_catch` `config.retry` spelling passes. Kept.

PM mechanism assumption ②, measured: stored flows still heal. `AutomationEngine.canonicalizeFlow` replays with `includeRetired: true`, and its only exclusion (`CONVERSIONS_NOT_REPLAYED_AT_REHYDRATION`) is `flow-decision-mode-inclusive-explicit`, which is not in this family. `service-automation`'s `crud-config-aliases.test.ts` now pins both halves: `normalizeStackInput` hands `{ object, filters }` on as written, and `registerFlow` plus `execute` still query `crm_lead` with `{ id: 'L1' }`.

## A second producer: the metadata save door's flow fallback (`packages/metadata-protocol`)

This is outside the claim's file surface, so the landing spot and the reason are stated here. `saveMetaItem` canonicalizes a flow through the automation engine (the full chain, retired entries included). When no automation service is reachable, or the canonicalizer throws, it judges a fallback verdict body built with `applyConversionsToFlow(request.item)`, in the authoring posture. Under the #21982 ruling, that verdict must not depend on whether the host runs an automation service. Retiring these seven entries would have broken that: 9 tests in `protocol.save-flow-canonicalization.test.ts` went red, because the fallback now refused `filters` and `functionName` bodies that the canonicalizer heals.

The fix replays the chain the canonicalizer replays: `includeRetired: true`, minus the same default flip, listed beside it with its reason (`FLOW_FALLBACK_VERDICT_NOT_REPLAYED`, following the per-door exclusion pattern of the engine and the artifact door). With the fix, the fallback reaches the canonicalizer's verdict for every retired flow shape: the seven retired here, and those retired earlier that walk a flow, `flow-inert-keys-removed` (`flow.active` / `flow.template` / `nodes[].outputSchema` / `errorHandling.fallbackNodeId`) and `flow-node-wait-timeout-keys-removed` (`waitEventConfig.timeoutMs` / `onTimeout`). So this is a behaviour change on the fallback path. On a host with no automation service, a body carrying one of those older keys was refused 422 by its tombstone before this PR; it is now healed for the verdict and stored as submitted. That is what the service-backed path already did, and what #21982 asks for. A new pin beside the #21982 block (`flow.active` on a no-service host saves, stored raw) holds it. The 9 red tests are the before reading for the seven, and the after reading is green.

## The record and strict-exit suites

`page-component-visibility-to-visibleWhen` stays live, so the three suites that ride it (`stack-conversions-record.test.ts`, `stack-conversion-record-door.test.ts`, `validate-json-strict-exit.e2e.test.ts`) need no re-pointing. The wrong sentence at `validate-json-strict-exit.e2e.test.ts:63-65` is fixed: the conversion that retired is `page-header-subtitle-alias`.

## Pin sweep

The conversion ids and the old refusal wording were grepped across the whole repo. These pins were flipped to the new semantics:

- Spec: `builtin-node-config.test.ts`, `io-node-config.test.ts`, `schemaless-node-config.test.ts` and `sharing.test.ts`. Each now asserts the prescription text (`` `X` was removed in @objectstack/spec 18 `` plus `Use CANONICAL`). The `full` pin also asserts code `invalid_value`, a single issue, and no "Expected one of" text.
- Spec: `flow-builtin-node-config-keys.test.ts`. `defineStack` now refuses `STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` / 422 at `flows.0.nodes.1.config.filters`, and a stored body converted with `includeRetired` parses clean.
- Spec: `conversions.test.ts` and `region-walk.test.ts`. The rewrite cases run the data-at-rest posture.
- `service-automation`: `crud-config-aliases.test.ts`, as above.
- Comments that became false: `flow.test.ts`, the D3 entry `18.flow-script-subflow-config-undeclared-keys-refused`, and the reference page `schemaless-node-config.mdx`, which `gen:docs` regenerates from the docblock.

## Verification

Commands, exit codes and real readings are in the report comment on the card. Summary:

- `@objectstack/spec`: `test` 678 files / 20728 tests passed; `test:repo` 60 / 1029 passed; `typecheck` exit 0; `check:generated` all 14 artifacts up to date. The four ratchets show zero change, as expected for value and key narrowing on existing defs.
- Consumers: `service-automation` 186 files / 2486 tests passed; `lint` 139 / 6726 passed; `metadata-protocol` and `plugin-sharing` are in the report.
- Derived gate families: `dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`, 115 commands, reconciled with `--ran`.

## Acceptance notes

- Several executor comments in `service-automation` (`crud-nodes.ts`, `notify-node.ts`, `map-node.ts`, `subflow-node.ts`, `screen-nodes.ts`) and `lint` (`validate-flow-node-writes.ts`, `validate-readonly-flow-writes.ts`, `validate-expressions.ts`) still say an alias "is rewritten at load". That is still true of the seam those executors sit behind (flow rehydration), so they are left alone.
- The save door with an automation service heals a retired flow alias through the engine instead of refusing it. That was the case before this PR (and already holds for the earlier retired flow-node tombstones). The authoring funnel is the jurisdiction of `retiredFromLoadPath`.
